config.title: Write omit generic with keyof

intro.title: Write omit generic with keyof
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a TypeScript utility function called `omit` that creates a new object by excluding specified properties from an existing object. You will learn how to use the `keyof` operator to work with object keys as a union type, ensuring type safety. The core concept involves creating a generic function that uses mapped types and conditional types to filter out keys. By the end, you'll understand how to write reusable, type-safe utilities in TypeScript.
intro.usecase: The Omit utility type with keyof is essential when working with TypeScript in frontend applications where you need to create modified versions of existing types. For example, when building a user profile form, you might have a complete User type with sensitive fields like password or ssn, but need to create a safe version for display by omitting those fields. In dashboard components, you might omit certain configuration properties when passing data to child visualization widgets. This pattern also appears in API response transformations, where you strip internal metadata fields before sending data to the client, ensuring clean type safety throughout your application.

objectives: Construct a generic type that accepts an object type and a union of keys.
Apply the `keyof` operator to extract keys from an object type.
Implement a conditional type to exclude specified keys from the original object.
Integrate the `Exclude` utility type to filter keys within your generic.
Manipulate mapped types to produce a new object type with the remaining properties.
Initialize a type alias using your custom `Omit` generic.
Render a function that utilizes your custom `Omit` type for type-safe operations.
